text: Handled client retries and processor timeouts well: idempotency keys, a stored first result, and a pending state with later reconciliation.
State the trade-off before the implementation. You chose PostgreSQL for the idempotency store without comparing it to a cache on consistency and latency.
Give numbers. 'As fast as possible' is not a target; propose a p99 latency and an acceptable duplicate-charge rate.
Walked through a feature from database schema to API to UI and named who is affected at each layer.
Started designing the cart service immediately. Ask about traffic, consistency needs and users before drawing boxes.
Picked REST over GraphQL without comparing them. Say what you give up with each choice for this mix of clients.
Described a practical retrieval pipeline: chunking by document structure, hybrid keyword and vector retrieval, reranking, and citations in answers.
No answer for how retrieval quality is measured. Name recall@k or answer-faithfulness checks and how you would build a labeled set.
You said the support assistant 'worked well'. Give resolution rate, latency or cost numbers instead.
Did not discuss the cost and latency trade-off between larger models and caching or smaller models. State it before choosing.
Debugged from metrics and traces rather than guesswork, and defined what each alert should tell the on-call engineer.
Designed bounded retries with backoff and a dead-letter queue, and explained how poison messages are isolated.
Chose a queue over a cron-based scheduler without saying why. Compare delivery guarantees, operational cost and ordering before deciding.
Scale was 'a lot of jobs'. Put numbers on throughput, queue depth and the retry budget.
Opened with questions about who books appointments, how many clinics and which privacy rules apply before proposing a design.
Raised protected health data handling, audit logging and least-privilege access without being asked.
Past project outcomes were qualitative. Add measurable results such as time saved or error rate reduction.
Compared a single agent with a handoff workflow, explaining latency, debuggability and cost of each before choosing.
Designed narrow typed tools, confirmation before destructive actions and read-only tools for recall, limiting the agent's blast radius.
Proposed an offline evaluation set scored on task success and tool-call accuracy, a clear improvement over earlier interviews.
Results were still not quantified. Lead each project story with one number.
